results.correct_value: 7000 (gain_ft), matching the itinerary days 3,550 + 1,550 + 1,900 and loss_ft 7,050
results.evidence: A detailed Depot Creek report gives 2,350 ft at the road-end parking, +3,550 ft to Ouzel Lake, and +1,550 ft to the Redoubt Glacier saddle at 7,150 ft; the summit is 8,407 ft on topo-derived listings. The net rise from 2,350 ft to 8,407 ft alone is ~6,050 ft, so 5,450 ft is physically impossible; 5,450 is exactly day 1 + day 3, i.e. the day-2 carry to high camp was left out. A second report gives a ~2,300 ft trailhead and 5,700 ft lake, agreeing on the first leg.

dist_km is the ONE-WAY approach figure (14.5 km ~ 9 mi) while the itinerary miles are per day and sum to a round trip. 9 mi one way is consistent with the itinerary's 7.5 mi to Lake Ouzel + 2 mi to the saddle high camp (and its 9.5 mi hike-out). A one-way figure compared with a round-trip sum is not a contradiction.

results.fact: Time to reach Lake Ouzel camp

results.evidence: One party recorded 6h15 car to Lake Ouzel; another took 9.3 hours to Ouzel Lake (+3,550 ft) and then 3.2 hours to the 7,150 ft saddle; a third report (Mountaineers) mentions about 8 hours in heat. Patched the approach prose to a 6-9 hour range and its derived trailhead-to-high-camp total, and reworded the itinerary note to the same range without attributing it to reports.

results.fact: Whether September is part of the best/safe climbing window
results.evidence: The fields describe a Jul-Sep season with a best window of mid-July through August and a caveat that LATE September can be iced and bare (climate.fall itself says conditions deteriorate after early-mid September). patches.fact: turnaround and comms describe the Thunder Creek approach, not this route

results.fact: Whether the North Ridge is reached via Lucky Pass
results.correct_value: From the Borealis Glacier bivy, go around the glacial lake and across a short stretch of glacier to the foot of the North Ridge; Lucky Pass is only on the descent
results.evidence: The first-ascent account reached the ridge from an unnamed glacier north of Primus via a couloir off the North Klawatti side, not via Lucky Pass. A September 2012 party went east around Borealis Lake from camp to the north ridge crest, and a 2016 party climbed from the glacier base up the north ridge and descended the standard route to the Primus-Tricouni saddle. All agree Lucky Pass is the descent, not the way onto the ridge.

patches.fact: Whether the North Ridge is reached via Lucky Pass
